title: Private Console Tenant Safety Playbook — compact UI prototype for upgrades, cost guardrails, and quick-mitigations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, operator-focused 'Tenant Safety Playbook' surface inside the Private Console that combines upgrade safety indicators, cost delta previews, and one-click quick-mitigations for degraded tenants. The goal is to let SREs and platform engineers rapidly assess upgrade risk, preview cost/latency trade-offs, and trigger guarded mitigations (throttle, rollback, redirect to dedicated pool) without leaving the console.

Background and motivation:
- Ops teams currently bounce between the cluster status page, cost explorer, and runbooks when an upgrade or network event threatens tenant SLAs.
- We want a single, scannable surface that: 1) flags risk signals (KV cache cold starts, batch latency spikes, region saturation), 2) quantifies cost/latency impact of potential mitigations, and 3) surfaces safe quick actions with built-in confirmation and audit trails.

Personas:
- Platform SRE (primary): needs low-friction remediation and clear guardrails.
- Tenant owner (secondary): wants clarity on upgrade timing and potential cost/latency implications.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype shows a compact header card with risk score, top-3 contributing signals, and a cost-delta preview for the most likely mitigations.
- A collapsible action rail with three guarded actions (Throttle, Route to Dedicated, Pause Canary) including microcopy for side-effects and estimated token-cost impact.
- Audit/confirmation modal that documents the operator, reason, and automatic rollback window. Action execution should link to ENG runbook endpoints (placeholder links are fine for prototype).
- Metrics surfaced: estimated tokens/sec saved, expected p50/p95 latency change, and 7-day cost delta.
- Usability test: median time-to-decision <= 90s for SREs in internal sessions.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on the UX surface and copy; backend wiring (metrics, action APIs) is tracked in ENG-22301.
- We will not implement RBAC enforcement here; assume RBAC gating will be applied by engineering.

Design approach and trade-offs considered:
- Compact vs detailed: prioritize a one-line risk score + three signals for scanning; deeper telemetry accessible via a "Details" flyout to avoid clutter.
- Cost estimation fidelity: show an estimated range and explain uncertainty (low/medium/high confidence) rather than precise numbers when upstream metrics are incomplete.
- Action safety: each quick-mitigation must require two-step confirmation and show a time-limited auto-rollback suggestion. This increases clicks but reduces blast radius.

Flows & screens to prototype:
1) Tenant Safety Card (collapsed): risk score, top signal icons, cost-delta micro badge, "Investigate" and "Quick Actions" CTA.
2) Tenant Safety Card (expanded): inline sparkline for latency, cost delta bar, recent related incidents, and a link to the upgrade timeline.
3) Quick Action Rail: three actions with inline tooltips, estimated impact, and a preview button that simulates effects in a sandbox.
4) Confirmation modal: captures operator note, optional runbook reference, and checkbox to schedule auto-rollback. Changes are recorded in audit logs (mocked).

Prototype assets and artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/PRIVATE/tenant-safety-playbook-proto (internal link placeholder)
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Private+Tenant+Safety+Playbook (internal link placeholder)
- Design spec (internal Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1SafetyPlaybookProto (placeholder)

Metrics of success:
- Reduction in mean time-to-mitigation for tenant incidents by 25% in the pilot group.
- >80% positive rating from SREs in prototype usability sessions.
